note.question: Which combinations of collateral, programmable commitment, interest policy, and decentralized issuance can make a profit-seeking stablecoin maintain its peg?
note.overview: A monopolistic stablecoin issuer strategically chooses supply, interest, collateralization, and liquidation against forward-looking users whose demand and price satisfy an Euler equation. The paper compares commitment and time-consistent policies and then introduces competitive vault owners under decentralized issuance. Equilibrium selection, dynamic optimization, limited liability, and strategic dilution are central.

The paper compares commitment and time-consistent policies and then introduces competitive vault owners under decentralized issuance. Equilibrium selection, dynamic optimization, limited liability, and strategic dilution are central.

components.label: Rational-expectations stablecoin equilibrium under commitment or sequential policy
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Rational-expectations stablecoin equilibrium under commitment or sequential policy. Users' Euler equation, market clearing, issuer optimality, and limited liability jointly determine price and supply. The paper selects a positive-value monetary equilibrium rather than the collateral-value/nonmonetary equilibrium, characterizes a three-region target Markov policy under limited liability, and then solves a decentralized equilibrium in which free-entry vault owners earn zero issuance rents and the protocol chooses time-consistent fees.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors derive user demand from continuous-time utility maximization, rewrite the issuer's problem in seigniorage form, and solve the unlimited-liability benchmark analytically. Under limited liability they characterize target Markov policies using HJB equations, obtain a closed form for uncollateralized coins, and solve partial collateralization numerically. A one-step deviation demonstrates time inconsistency, after which vault-owner arbitrage and free entry deliver the decentralized equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At date 0 the protocol chooses a constant collateralization ratio phi. In continuous time, exogenous stablecoin-demand index A_t follows diffusion with downward Poisson jumps, and users choose consumption and stablecoin holdings, generating a dynamic demand equation. A centralized protocol chooses issuance or repurchase, stablecoin interest, and liquidation either under date-0 commitment or sequential reoptimization. Under decentralized issuance, phi is immutable; atomistic vault owners continuously choose minting, burning, or default while protocol equity holders set interest and vault fees sequentially.
